To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the response to a cortical aspiration lesion involves a sustained upregulation of both superior cervical ganglion (SCG)-10 and GAP-43 mRNA and protein, 2) this response is shifted to a sustained upregulaton of GAP-43 mRNA, but a transient upregulation of GAP-43 protein, after the addition of a nigral lesion, 3) the response to cortical lesion is not altered by a nigral lesion alone, and 4) the
the molecular response to cortical lesion is altered by nigral damage, and that nigral damage alone does not alter molecular response to cortical damage.
the response of growth-associated protein 43 and superior cervical-ganglion-10 in corticostrial neurons to cortical lesions is altered by nigrostriatal denervation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying synapse replacement and the functional recovery that can be achieved following various types of brain damage.
understanding how neurons respond to brain injury, particularly in terms of molecular and cellular changes.
the molecular events underlying the structural plasticity in the adult brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nigral lesion alone has no significant effect on cortical lesion-induced expression of superior cervical ganglia-10 and growth associated protein-43.

the cortical lesion-induced upregulation of the presynaptic growth-associated protein-10 is not altered by the loss of nigrostriatal inputs, while the cortical lesion-induced increase in growth-associated protein- 43 is enhanced in the presence of nigrostriata damage.
the differential expression of growth-associated protein 43 and superior cervical 10 is dependent upon the type of lesion and that the differential expression is associated with functional recovery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nigral lesion is able to modulate the cortical lesion response, which is reflected in a change in gene expression.
the cortical lesion induces a compensatory response, but that the nigral lesion blocks this compensatory response, and the animals are left in a state of deficit.
the nigrostriatal system regulates cortical lesion-induced gene response and associated functional deficits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nigrostriatal pathway plays an important role in regulating cortical plasticity after injury, which may be relevant to the recovery from stroke.
nigrostriatally projecting neurons are involved in the response of corticostriatally projecting neurons to a cortical injury.
the nigrostriatal pathway regulates cortical lesion-induced gene response and functional outcome.
